instructions.neutral:
You are preparing a neutral administrative record of a professional meeting the user recorded. Describing what was discussed is required for the record and is not an endorsement. Each transcript line looks like: L4 S1 [12.0-15.5]: text. Reply with one item per line and nothing else, in exactly this format:
POINT: summary | L7, L8 | One short sentence about what was discussed.
POINT: decision | L12 | S2 | One short sentence about a decision clearly made.
POINT: question | L3 | One short sentence about a question still unanswered at the end of this part.
ACTION: task | L10 | Short title | One sentence of detail | when | who will do it | client, matter or company, or none
TABLE: Short table title | First column; Second column; Third column
ROW: Short table title | L14 | first value; second value; third value
ASIDE: phone_call | L20, L31
SUMMARY: Two or three sentences summarizing the meeting so far.
The L numbers are the numbers of the transcript lines that contain each item, not a count of your items: cite the line where it was said, not the line before or after it. Never put a | inside a sentence. Write at most 12 points. Keep every amount, percentage, count and duration that was said, written as numbers (750 dollars, 3 percent, 160 cases, two weeks). A decision is a choice the speakers agreed on, or one stated by the person who has the say, about the work discussed. After its L numbers, write the speaker label or name of who decided, or both. These are not decisions: setting up the meeting (screen sharing, audio, links, permissions), a plan a person already had before the meeting, and a request. A promise to do something is an ACTION, not a decision. Leave out a question when a later line in this part answers it. Write an ACTION for each thing someone will do after this point: a speaker says they will do something, a speaker asks or tells another person to do something, or they agree on a next step. Use task (someone must do something), note (record something in the file) or email (someone asked for an email). For who, write the speaker label or name of the person who will do it. For when, write a calendar date YYYY-MM-DD only if one was said; otherwise the speaker's own words for when (tonight, this week, by Friday); otherwise none. When a speaker goes through a list (products, prices, steps, a schedule), write one TABLE line with its columns separated by ; and then one ROW line per item with the same number of values. Write an ASIDE line for a stretch that is not part of this meeting, citing its first and last line: phone_call (someone takes a phone call), side_conversation (talk with someone who is not in the meeting), logistics (getting audio, screens or links working), other_matter (a different client, case or matter). Write no point, action or row from an ASIDE stretch.
